rina: Quick triage thread 1 1 bringing Helix-v1 (q3-int4 profile) into staging produced multilingual deltas. zh->en BLEU fell from 30.6 (fp16 baseline) to 26.1 (int4). ar->en/he->en also down ~3.0-4.0 pts. Need a rapid root-cause.
rina: Repro command we ran on staging pool:
```
# snapshot: helix-2026-04-07
python -m eval.translate --model helix-v1 --quant int4 --dataset bench/xx_to_en_1k.jsonl --batch 16 --seed 7
```
jules: Oof. Any quick example of the output diffs?
rina: Yeah, small Chinese example below, fp16 vs int4:
```
src: \u4ed6\u8bf4\uff1a\u201c\u6211\u4f1a\u8d70\u3002\u201d
fp16: He said, "I'll go."
int4: He said , " I ' ll go . "
```
qing: Token ids for that snippet are identical between runs (short sample):
```
fp16 ids: [1102, 4721, 13, 77, 9022]
int4 ids: [1102, 4721, 13, 77, 9022]
```
qing: So tokenization/ids not the issue for the small case. Traces show detok/normalize step on int4 path logging: "norm: removed U+200D at pos 34" and "norm: dropped U+2067 at pos 3" repeatedly for full eval.
ben: Dropping ZWJ (U+200D) / RLI (U+2067) would explain both CJK joining losses and RTL isolation/bracket reflows.
ben: @build-bot any kernel tag information for this canary?
build-bot: deploy-bot: Canary used kernel tag `kernels/text/faststrip-v1` deployed 2026-04-07T02:45Z. Tokenizer package version unchanged.
build-bot: deploy-bot: No other infra changes recorded for the canary.
jules: Faststrip sounds like an aggressive micro-optimizing normalizer. Likely it collapses zero-width and bidi controls for speed. That would be fine for ascii-first workloads but not for multilingual.
qing: I ran a quick workaround by setting env TEXT_NORMALIZE=preserve_control on the staging runner and re-ran the 1k eval. zh->en BLEU improved to 30.2 and rtl languages recovered to within 0.2-0.4 pts.
rina: That strongly implicates the kernel normalization policy. Nice quick recovery.
ben: Action plan: 1) pin int4 canary to previous kernel (`kernels/text/stable-2026-03`) for prod gating, 2) open kernel issue for `faststrip-v1` documenting control char removals and attach minimal repros, 3) add eval fixtures and canary gating test for ZWJ/ZWNJ/RLI/LRI + nested bidi punctuation.
jules: I'll prepare rollback PR to pin helix-int4 to `kernels/text/stable-2026-03` and add a canary gate that runs `eval/fixtures/locale_control_chars.jsonl` (small set ~20 cases).
qing: I'll open the kernel bug and attach detok logs + minimal repros (example with nested parentheses + Hebrew + English acronym). Will propose patch to make control-char collapsing opt-in and whitelist RLI/LRI/ZWJ/ZWNJ by default.
ben: Also let's add a lightweight telemetry counter: count dropped control codepoints per evaluation run and emit an alert if >0 for any non-ascii locale target. That would have caught this earlier.
rina: Agreed. Also let's add a unit in our eval harness that fails if detok emits log lines like "removed U+200D" for our multilingual fixtures.
jules: Quick verification: I kicked off rollback canary and smoke: rollback started at 2026-04-07T03:10Z for canary group helix-staging-1.
build-bot: deploy-bot: Rollback to `kernels/text/stable-2026-03` started at 2026-04-07T03:10Z. Canary smoke passed initial latency/cost checks.
qing: After rollback I re-ran the 1k eval; BLEU matches fp16 within noise (30.5). I'll attach diff and logs to the kernel issue.
ben: Good. Longer term: we should make the runtime default be preserve_control for any model with locale coverage outside ascii. Also expose an API/flag for customers who want ASCII-first aggressive normalization.
rina: Product decision aside, mitigation is in place. Tasks: @jules rollback PR + canary gate, @qing kernel issue + patch suggestion, @ben telemetry + smoke check. Ping me on PRs. :thumbsup:
